title: Cornyn Slams Brakes on Trump Judicial Nominee as GOP Lame-Duck Sprint Hits Obstacle
snippet: Texas Sen. John Cornyn blocked DOJ official T. Elliot Gaiser's lifetime judicial appointment, criticizing the White House for trying to "jam" an inexperienced, out-of-state candidate into a Dallas federal seat.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump's last-ditch push to fill federal court vacancies before Democrats assume control of the Senate suffered a fresh setback Wednesday, after a key Senate Republican stepped in to block a White House judicial pick in his home state.

Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn (R-Texas) withheld his support for Department of Justice official T. Elliot Gaiser, effectively preventing the 37-year-old nominee from appearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee for a confirmation hearing on a federal trial judge seat in Dallas.

'Not From Texas'

Under longstanding Senate custom, home-state senators hold informal veto power over district court nominees through a practice known as returning a "blue slip." By refusing to submit his blue slip, Cornyn effectively halted Gaiser's path forward.

Cornyn pulled no punches when explaining his resistance to the White House effort.

"He's not from Texas," Cornyn said. "He has no trial experience, and the White House was trying to jam him down our throat without adequate vetting for a lifetime job."

Gaiser, a former Ohio solicitor general who previously clerked for conservative Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito, currently leads the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel. Cornyn has instead pushed the administration to nominate Steve Fahey, a former federal prosecutor based in Texas, noting that the White House has recently shown interest in the alternative pick.

Tensions Within the GOP

The intra-party dispute triggered a sharp rebuke from fellow Texas Republican Sen. Ted Cruz, who backed Gaiser's nomination and warned that time is running out before the current congressional session ends on January 3.

Cruz cautioned that starting over with a new candidate would make it impossible to clear mandatory FBI background checks before control of the chamber flips. "If the Senate Judiciary Committee does not move Gaiser forward, the people of Texas will pay the price because it will effectively give the judicial seat to the Democrats, who will keep it vacant in perpetuity," Cruz said in a statement.

The showdown marks the latest instance of home-state Republican pushback derailing White House judicial picks during the post-election transition period. Earlier this month, the administration rescinded U.S. District Judge Lee Rudofsky's nomination to the 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals following pushback from Arkansas senators, replacing him with Arkansas Supreme Court Justice J. Cody Hiland.

Despite the friction over Gaiser, the White House maintained in a statement that it expects to confirm all of Trump's pending judicial nominees before the end of the year.
